extra_misconceptions.fact: Landscape architects design site grading, drainage, circulation paths, and outdoor structures alongside the planting palette.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A landscape architect only selects flowers and shrubs after civil engineers and building architects finish all outdoor site grading.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Trees and shrubs take years to reach mature canopy heights, so comparing the plan reveals how young plants will frame spaces.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Visiting a newly planted landscape immediately after installation shows the true spatial enclosure intended by the designer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unforeseen bedrock, buried utilities, or soil conditions often require field adjustments documented only on as-built drawings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every feature visible on a finished public park matches the original construction drawing without field modifications.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Draftsmen rotate site plans to fit rectangular sheets, so you must locate the North arrow to align the plan with a compass.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reading a landscape plan from top to bottom always faces due north regardless of how the drawing sheet fits the border.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your field observations if you walk the completed site before orienting the North arrow on the printed plan?
Which plan symbol distinguishes a proposed grading contour line from an existing utility line on a landscape architect's drawing?
What field note best documents where mature tree canopies or post-construction paths now differ from the original site drawing?
Why is it dangerous to step into dense ornamental ground cover or retaining wall ledges while reading a folded blueprint?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Paved plazas and turf areas need a minimum one to two percent cross-slope so surface runoff drains away from walkways.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Flat lawns and level concrete plazas require zero slope so rainwater can soak straight down into the underlying soil.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Deciduous trees on the south or west side block summer sun with full foliage and drop leaves in winter to admit solar warmth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Planting evergreen trees on the south side of a patio provides ideal winter warmth while blocking hot summer afternoon sun.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Paving changes, subtle grade shifts, overhead tree canopies, and low shrub massings define separate outdoor spaces without walls.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Outdoor rooms require solid masonry walls or tall wooden fences on all four sides to separate active areas from quiet zones.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tall structures require medium or large canopy trees nearby to step down vertical scale and transition the building to the ground.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Lining a three-story civic building exclusively with dwarf two-foot shrubs creates balanced architectural proportion.

extra_socratic_questions: What visual cue at a public park entrance tells first-time visitors where to walk without relying on directional text signs?
Which physical indicator separates a primary circulation walkway from a secondary strolling path in a public plaza design?
At what times of day should you record shadow patterns across outdoor seating areas to verify full sun and shade variety?
Under what condition does poor surface grading beside a shaded concrete walkway create a slip hazard for pedestrians?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Plants must be spaced by their mature canopy spread so roots and branches have room to grow without constant heavy shearing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Shrubs should be spaced according to the width of their nursery pots so the planting bed looks full on installation day.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ground covers suppress erosion and reduce mowing, but they still require edging, weeding during establishment, and watering.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ground cover plants eliminate all future weeding and maintenance once their runners spread across a bare soil slope.

extra_misconceptions.fact: USDA zones measure only average minimum winter temperatures, while soil pH, clay compaction, and afternoon heat govern survival.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any tree rated for your USDA cold hardiness zone will thrive anywhere in your yard regardless of soil drainage or sun exposure.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Plant texture refers to the visual size, spacing, and surface quality of leaves and twigs rather than bark roughness or thorns.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Fine-textured plants have tiny delicate flowers, whereas coarse-textured plants have rough bark and thorny woody stems.

extra_socratic_questions: What site factors beyond your USDA hardiness zone must you verify at a local nursery before choosing five shrubs and five trees?
What visual effect does pairing coarse-textured hosta leaves against fine-textured ornamental grasses have on perceived space?
What measurement on a nursery plant tag prevents you from spacing young shrubs so closely that they overcrowd within five years?
Why is it dangerous to clip branch samples from unfamiliar roadside shrubs without first checking for toxic sap or hidden thorns?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts must always obtain explicit permission from the appropriate site authority before measuring or surveying any grounds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Measuring a public building entry for a merit badge sketch does not require property manager permission if the lot is open.

extra_misconceptions.fact: In landscape architecture, a mixer space is a widened plaza outside an entrance where arriving and departing people gather.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A mixer space is an equipment staging pad where contractors mix concrete and mortar during public building renovations.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Site plans show horizontal distances, so field tapes must be pulled taut and held level when measuring across sloped ground.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling a cloth or fiberglass measuring tape loosely along undulating turf gives an accurate horizontal plan distance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bollards, raised curbs, and buffer planting beds keep vehicle drop-off loops clear of pedestrian gathering plazas at entries.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Widening vehicle drop-off lanes right up to the front doors is the safest way to improve a busy school or church entrance.

extra_socratic_questions: Why do landscape architects sketch redesign concepts on tracing paper overlays rather than drawing directly on the measured base map?
What spatial function distinguishes a pedestrian mixer space outside a building entrance from an ordinary transit sidewalk?
What scale ratio allows a 100-foot school entry driveway and sidewalk system to fit cleanly onto a standard 11-by-17-inch sheet?
Where should a Scout buddy team position a lookout while stretching a measuring tape across an active school bus drop-off lane?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every state regulates the title and practice of landscape architecture through an LAAB degree, supervised experience, and the LARE.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Anyone who completes a college horticulture course can legally stamp public site grading plans as a landscape architect.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Career pathways span municipal park systems, urban planning agencies, environmental restoration firms, and civil engineering teams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Landscape architects work almost exclusively for private homeowners designing backyard patios, pools, and flower borders.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Graduates must log years of mentored internship under a licensed practitioner and pass all four sections of the national LARE exam.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating with a Bachelor of Landscape Architecture degree immediately grants a state license without further examination.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Candidates must budget for studio drafting supplies, CAD hardware, multi-part LARE exam fees, state license dues, and continuing ed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tuition is the only significant expense required to transition from a university landscape program into licensed practice.

extra_socratic_questions: What sequence of accredited education, mentored internship hours, and national examination is required for state licensure?
Which legal responsibility separates a state-licensed landscape architect from an unlicensed residential garden designer?
What financial categories beyond university tuition must you record when calculating the total cost of entering this profession?
Why is a licensed professional required to stamp public grading and retaining wall plans before construction crews break ground?
